back: The nationalist complaint that Italy had been cheated at the 1919 peace settlement, especially over Dalmatia and Fiume.
Violence by Fascist squads (blackshirts) against socialists, unions and cooperatives, tolerated by police and funded by landowners.

front: When did the March on Rome take place and what was the outcome?
back: 27-28 October 1922; the King refused martial law and Mussolini became prime minister on 31 October.
Two thirds of the seats to the party with at least 25 per cent of the votes.

front: Who was Matteotti and what happened to him?
back: A Socialist deputy who denounced Fascist violence in May 1924 and was murdered by Fascists in June 1924.
The walk-out of opposition deputies from the Chamber after the Matteotti murder in 1924.

front: Why did the King allow Mussolini to take power?
back: He feared civil war and army disloyalty and thought Mussolini could be tamed by office.
Ex-servicemen, nationalists, landowners, industrialists and many middle-class people who feared socialism.

front: How was the dictatorship created between 1922 and 1926?
back: The Acerbo Law, the 1924 election, the speech of 3 January 1925 and the laws of 1925-26 against opposition, press and unions.
